stem:
Rajni, a class 10 student has set up the apparatus as shown in the figures.

The four beakers each contain a glass rod and the following contents:
Beaker I: 20 mL water + \(\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4\)
Beaker II: 20 mL water + \(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3\)
Beaker III: 20 mL water + anhydrous \(\text{CuSO}_4\)
Beaker IV: 20 mL \(\text{CuSO}_4\) solution + Zn granules

Which of the following observations is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Temperature will not change in beaker IV as redox reactions are exothermic.

options.label: B
options.text: Temperature of beakers I, II and III will be raised as dissolution of salts is an exothermic process.

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature will rise only in beaker II as redox reactions are exothermic.

options.label: D
options.text: Temperature of beakers III and IV will be raised but temperature of beakers I and II will fall.

stem:
Marble chips or calcium carbonate react with hydrochloric acid as:
\(\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\)
The reaction is carried out twice and the following graphs were obtained (volume of \(\text{CO}_2\) released in cm\(^3\) versus time in minutes). Curve for Experiment II rises more steeply and reaches its plateau sooner than the curve for Experiment I, but both curves level off at the same final volume of \(\text{CO}_2\).

Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Reaction is faster in experiment II.

options.label: B
options.text: Same amount of marble chips and hydrochloric acid is used for both the experiments.

options.label: C
options.text: Marble chips taken in experiment II are smaller in size than the marble chips taken in experiment I.
